surfaces.part: ground tile surface (dusty packed earth with pebbles)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full-bleed 64x48 flat ground texture with a uniform width of 64 on every row. It has no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no front face. The brown and grey-brown patches, pebbles and dark crack marks repeat every 16 rows and every 16 columns, so it is a seamless top-down terrain pattern. As a terrain tile it is meant to be flat, so having no front face is expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch of the same kind as the grass and paving references. Its earth ramp runs from a pale dust highlight through grey-tan mids to dark brown, with rust-brown speckle clusters on top, so it reads as about 6 steps against the references' roughly 5. The measured facts support this: 8 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, and 0% near-flat coverage, which matches the references. There are no flat 5x5 areas; the whole surface carries grain, pebble dots and mottled patches. As a ground tile it has no sticker outline, and the 0% near-neutral dark edge share shows no black line. The surface is slightly noisy and its clusters are less structured than the paving stones, but it is not thinner or flatter than the references and would sit acceptably beside them.
